faq.a1: Baram(바람) is a lightweight desktop WYSIWYG markdown editor built with Tauri 2.0, React, and Tiptap/ProseMirror. It combines Typora-style "disappearing syntax" WYSIWYG editing with bidirectional links and AI-powered writing assistance.
faq.a2: Baram runs on macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows (x64 and ARM), and Linux (x64).
faq.a3: Yes. Baram is free and open source software, licensed under the Apache License 2.0.
faq.a4: Yes. Baram's core principle is lossless roundtrip fidelity — when you open a markdown file, edit it, and save it, your content is preserved exactly. No proprietary format, no hidden database. When you use layout features such as table column resizing or diagram sizing, Baram stores that metadata as plain, visible markdown comments right in the file — standard markdown that other editors simply ignore.
faq.a5: Yes. Open Settings > Keybindings to see all shortcuts organized by category. Click Edit on any shortcut, press the new key combination, and click Apply.
faq.a6: Baram currently supports English and Korean for the entire user interface — menus, dialogs, settings, and all UI elements.

features.ai.d: Inline AI edits (Cmd+J), Ghost Text autocomplete, and AI chat — powered by Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, or local Ollama.
features.journal.d: A diary-focused daily-notes space with calendar, photos, and streaks — plus an atomic-notes space where a capture's tags are its address: tag it with a note's name and it lands inside that note.
features.light.d: ~10MB binary, instant startup, low memory. A desktop app that feels like the wind.
features.links.d: [[links]] with autocomplete, backlinks, block references, tags — and a visual graph of your knowledge.
features.pdf.d: Read PDFs in place — find, zoom, page and highlight panels. Highlight a sentence or a figure, then cite it in a note: the reference renders as the quote, or as the cropped region of the page.
features.plugins.d: Install community plugins from a built-in, capability-gated marketplace — sandboxed by default, with signed withdrawal checks. Or build your own with the plugin API.
features.rich.d: KaTeX math, code blocks with highlighting for 14+ languages, Mermaid diagrams, SVG blocks, and advanced tables with cell merge.
features.roundtrip.d: MD → editor → MD preserves your document exactly, including markup Baram does not render itself. Your notes are text files in your own folders — open them in any editor, today or in ten years.
features.tasks.d: Every checkbox in your vault, indexed. Four states, due and scheduled dates, priority, repeat rules and time tracking — written as Obsidian-compatible fields you never have to type. An agenda buckets it all by Overdue, Today, and This week.
features.title: Features
features.vault.d: Open multiple vaults, folders, and files side by side — each with its own tree, tabs, and settings — and switch layouts instantly with perspectives.
features.wysiwyg.d: Markdown delimiters show only when your cursor enters the range — and vanish when you leave. What remains is beautifully styled text.
hero.sub: A lightweight, beautiful WYSIWYG markdown editor with AI integration — syntax disappears as you type, and your notes stay text files any editor can open.
hero.title: Like the wind, light and free.
install.noteMacFolder: macOS asks once for access to folders such as Documents, Desktop, Downloads, or iCloud. Grant it and the permission persists, including across updates.
install.noteMacLead: macOS: Baram is signed with an Apple Developer ID certificate and notarized by Apple, so it opens without a Gatekeeper warning. On first launch macOS still asks to confirm an app downloaded from the internet — that prompt is normal and appears for every notarized app.
install.noteWin: Windows: if SmartScreen blocks the app, choose More info → Run anyway.
install.s1: Grab the installer for your platform from the download button above, or browse all builds on the releases page.
install.s2: macOS: open the .dmg and drag Baram into Applications. Windows: run the setup wizard. Linux: install the .deb/.rpm, or make the AppImage executable and run it.
install.s3: Launch Baram and open any folder or markdown file — no account, no setup.
